utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we have the witness, are there any procedural matters that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this bench?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I believe there was a misunderstanding when Mr. Stojanovic was cross-examining Groenewegen. At the end, the Prosecution moved to introduce their exhibit list into evidence and Mr. Stojanovic introduced an exhibit for the Prosecution, I think it was P48. We do not wish to have that piece of evidence introduced and he withdraws that request to have that exhibit introduced. If that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's quite all right. I think there was a misunderstanding because we -- I believe that it's a good piece of evidence to impeach the credibility of that witness but if you want to withdraw this evidence, we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So this piece of the evidence is withdrawn from the Defence team's list.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there anything else? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we had a -- another witness available in case we ended early today with our current witness. However, he has become ill and is now back at the hotel and so we may, if we are able to finish early, we unfortunately won't have a witness for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. I'm very sorry to hear that, that that witness is not in good health, and I wish him a speedy recovery. That means that if we finish that witness, we'll call it a day. And I think we have to make the best use of the time available to us. Maybe we will spend about 20 and 30 minutes on the procedural matters. There are several issues that this bench would like to discuss with the parties, concerning the scheduling and the other procedural matters. Is that agreeable to everybody?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the witness? Yes, Mr. Blagojevic? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, I wish to strongly stress my concern here because of the way that the trial is proceeding. As far as I'm concerned, I have to bear the situation that has been imposed on me. The Defence has been imposed on me, which makes it illegal, and there is not even a minimum of responsibility as far as my position is concerned. If we take my situation from the 8th of July, you can see how much that was present then when questions were being asked regarding the witness testimony of Mr. Mandzic. Questions that were being asked were questions chosen by them. These are not as far as I'm concerned essential questions and they do not touch upon the situations that I believe should be the case to represent, to present my role in those times, and the situation began very well to demonstrate to what an extent, through various questions and answers, my situation is obvious and the situation of the people that I had under my command. In order to reduce my concern and anxiety which has been increasing from one day to the next, in order to resolve this situation, which objectively does not depend upon me, the only thing I can do is to come out with this, what I am doing now, because I do not think that currently the way things are proceeding, there will not be an objective impression of my role and the role of people under my command. It will not give the real truth, the real accurate picture. It can only create a series of speculations that are to my detriment and I am sorry but I really cannot accept this. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Blagojevic, we have a witness waiting outside the courtroom and we have already decided and agreed by everybody that we'll spend a period of time, maybe 30 minutes, to discuss those procedural matters. I will turn to you at that period. Do you agree with it? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] I agree with that, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Now, could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Issa please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Ms. Issa: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Captain Van Duijn just to quickly refresh your memory I believe we left off yesterday evening where you indicated that the transport of the refugees stopped in the late evening on the 12th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, earlier, sir, you had said that you'd heard that the refugees were being forced into the buses, they were being kicked and beaten. Can you indicate who reported that to you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few of my soldiers that were standing near the sides of the buses, but I saw that myself as well, not that they were kicked when they entered the buses but at one stage there was a Serb soldier in black uniform that more or less strangled a young boy from about 13 or 14 years old and only with the help of Captain Mane I could get the Serb soldier in the black uniform to go away so I'd heard some stories from my soldiers but also I'd seen it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe, elaborate a little bit on exactly what you saw, when you say more or less strangled a boy?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a boy standing with his family in the middle of the crowd, waiting to get on to one of the buses and suddenly one of the Serb soldiers in the black uniform came up -- I hadn't seen him there before, and he said something in Serbo-Croatian, I didn't understand it, but I got the impression that he wanted the boy to get out of the crowd so he could single him out as well and he grabbed him by the throat and tried to pull him out of the crowd but there were two or three people in between them, so the boy was being grabbed by the throat and pulled towards the Serb soldier and when I saw that, I took Captain Mane with me and said get this soldier away from here because as we agreed, when the Muslims were standing in a crowd, we would stand in the middle and the Serb soldiers would stand behind us, more or less 15 metres behind our position and Captain Mane said well, you're right and he took the guy in the black uniform away from that position. And the boy was left with his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, towards the end you indicated that we were towards the end of the evening. Did you speak with Mane again that evening?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the end of the transports, Mane stated to me that that was the end of the night but tomorrow the transports would continue again and that day would go to Bratunac and celebrate, celebrate the victory, and he also said that he wanted my pistol. I hadn't had the pistol with me. It was locked up in the APC like I told before and then we went over to the APCs but the APC was empty already. That's the last conversation I had with Mane. Then I saw that the men were taken away by the little lorry which I'd seen before, bringing the bread, from that stage I went back to the UN compound. Mane had told me that the next day they would be there about 8.30 to continue with the transports again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And when you went back to the UN compound, did you see anything there?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just before I arrived at the compound, a little bit south of the compound on the road, there was a roll call being held by the Serbs and it got my attention because the man, the Serb soldier I knew as Stalin by his code name was in front of the Serb troops, must have been about 60 or 70 Serb soldiers in that roll call and Stalin was in front of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before we move on to the 13th of July, just very briefly, sir, yesterday you mentioned you saw Nikolic speaking to Stalin. Can you explain how you knew it was Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Mane, because we heard more or less overheard a conversation on the radio, Serb radio, Mane explained to me that that was his commander, Stalin on the radio. Later that day, he said that Stalin was coming to visit, and when Stalin and Nikolic came to that location, I -- there was a sort of combination of recognising Major Nikolic because he was a well known figure in the enclave, and Mane explaining to me that that was his commander Stalin and Major Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said, sir, that after speaking to Captain Groen, you went to Potocari to assist the refugees. Did anyone go with you? This is earlier in the day on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And moving on, sir, to the 13th of July, 1995, can you tell us what happened in that morning?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After having slept a few hours, I was at the location of the transports where I'd left Lieutenant Koster, which -- who had taken over from me for the night. I met with him and spoke with him about the situation of the night. He told me that the refugees were still very panicky and it was a lot of situations that night that were more or less started by panic, someone would stand up and walk in the direction, and other people would wake up got up as well and walked in the same direction, not knowing what was going on but purely by the panic they felt. There was an incident of a man that had hung himself during the night and another man that had injured himself, hit himself on the head with a rock, to get this injury more or less to be treated as a wounded person so that he hoped that he would get a better treatment out of that, being wounded. So we more or less spoke about the night, spoke about the position of our APCs that we had planned the night before on the first day of the transport, to make a sort of channel on the road to have a little bit of more control over the crowd of refugees so they would not so easily fall down on the ground and be trampled on by the other refugees so that was more or less the discussion that we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say were you going to make a little bit of a channel, can you clarify that? With what?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: With our APCs, we put two APCs on each side of the road, two APCs in front that would form more or less a V shape tunnel which the refugees would enter on the broadside, on the wide side of the channel so that we did not need that much -- that many soldiers to keep the crowd calm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened, sir, when you -- or what did you do when you took over from Lieutenant Koster?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I just had taken over from Lieutenant Koster. We were surprised that the Serb buses already were arriving and we could see the drivers from the buses gathering together and waiting for things to come more or less asking us for what to do, and at that time I had a short conversation with Koster about this and I decided to already start with the transports, to prevent that the men were separated from their families and to prevent that the buses and the trucks would be crowded with refugees and so that was in my -- was my idea that we could keep the family as best as we could, we keep them together. I remember that Lieutenant Koster more or less asked me, well, is this a good idea? But we, as I remember we left it at that and he left from my location and I decided to go ahead with that plan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And how long did you do this before the Serb soldiers returned to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I remember, the Serb soldiers came to our location about 8.30, much like Mane stated before, and it must have been an hour, an hour and a half that we could keep the families together, keep the men with their families and I'm very glad that the Dutch NIOD Report also was able to find men that -- in that precious one and a half hour, were able to get out of the enclave without being singled out by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And can you describe, sir, what happened to the refugees and the families when the Serb soldiers returned at 8.30?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that moment on, and I remember that Mane was more or less baffled that we already had started, from that moment on, the Serbs took total control again and the men were singled out again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you describe the scene, sir, after all the refugees had been transported out of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looked like the scene I saw on the 11th, the southern part of Srebrenica was totally abandoned. The scene on the factory site was also empty, when you compare it to the days, the two days before, but there were a lot of personal belongings scattered all around the factory site. The refugees had left blankets, had left bags with potatoes, had left photos, all sorts of belongings that they had left there. There was garbage, of course, a lot of garbage but also a lot of personal belongings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any refugees at all that were left?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, the only refugees I knew that were still in the enclave were a few that were walking but that was only maybe five or ten that were still making the route to the buses. And the men that were gathered in the location as we know as the white house, that was just across the road near the entrance of the UN compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, referring then to Prosecutor's Exhibit 20.6/A, if you can look at that, look at your screen, can you identify what is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the white house I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything different that you see in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were there, there was a much more bushes and trees and also covered in leaves so you could really see the front lawn. You can now see only the little fence that was standing in front of the white house. There was also a lot of bushes and trees there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see at the white house on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The white house itself was packed with men. I managed to get a peek inside of the house. I could see that the house was really packed with men and a few of them were sitting just in front of the house with their backs against the wall of the house and in front of the house in the lawn, it was covered with also personal belongings, bags, photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe the appearance of the men at the white house?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were very scared. Of course it was warm so they were very warm as well. But you could see that they were very scared. They were quiet. And they were -- you could see really see that they were very, very scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. How old approximately were these men?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It varied from very young men to men about maybe 60, 65 years of old -- of age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Can you provide us with an age range, just in general?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Average age must have been around 35 or something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You indicated, sir, that you saw some personal belongings on the lawn of the -- in the front of the white house. Can you describe exactly what it is that you saw?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw bags, I saw pictures, and later on I also saw passports. At first, I thought someone had forgot or maybe lost it so I started to assemble identity papers, the passports, but then later on, when I had a both of my pockets were full with passports, I then went over to Captain Mane who was there as well, and I'd ask him about why the passports were spread on the lawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And what did Captain Mane say to you when you asked him about the passports on the lawn?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confronted him with his explanation about the men being singled out which he had told me the day before, about wanting to check if the men were war criminals, and I confronted him with that, because if they didn't have their passports they could easily have given a false name or something and then his system of trying to check who was a war criminal and who was not would not work, and he more or less laughed at me and said, "Well, don't make a fuss about it because they don't need those passports any more." So that was more or less the moment that I really knew that something really bad was going to happen. Of course, when you see men being teared from their families, you know that that is not the way a normal life should be lived but there was a war going on and terrible things happened there, but at that time when I saw the passports and knew that Mane said that they wouldn't need the passports any more, I knew that they had a very dark future ahead of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- was there any attempt at this point to accompany the men?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I did two things. I radioed our headquarters and stressed that we really should accompany the buses with which the men would be transported, and I tried to get in the bus myself but that ended when I was being held at gunpoint by the guy that was standing, Serb soldier that was standing near the entrance of the buses, and he pushed a Kalashnikov rifle in my belly and Mane took me buy the soldiers and pulled me away from there and said, just don't do it, you're not going in the bus. So that's not an option.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If we can then -- we are almost nearing the end of the examination, sir, if we can then briefly go back to April of 1995, I understand that you were a commander on two observation points at that point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area I was responsible for, we are had two observation posts, Romeo and Quebec. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were these observation posts located?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the north eastern part of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you briefly explain what observations you made in relation to Serbian -- the Serb troops that you saw at that time?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few of bunkers or locations where the Serbs were located and we could see what they were doing over there and that's what my soldiers also reported shootings or whatever happened, they reported in the normal way and we also had contact near OP Romeo with a Serb bunker that was really close to the border of the enclave, and we even visited sometimes that bunker to try and get some information from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And did you notice anything different about the Serbian troops during that period?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April, we saw that new soldiers, other soldiers than we had seen in the months earlier, were coming to that bunker and the difference between the new and the old soldiers was that the new soldiers were better equipped, they had rifles that were newer, they had complete uniforms on, they were younger, shaven, clean shaven every day so that was really a difference with the older soldiers we had seen in the previous months before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, very briefly, sir, did you observe during that period from your position at these two observation posts Muslim forces within the enclave?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had also next to the contacts we had with the Serb forces we also had contacts with Muslim forces and one of the contacts was Naser Sabanovic who was a commander in the northern part of the enclave and who lived near OP Quebec and I had several conversations with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know how the Muslim forces were armed?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were armed with rifles and occasionally a rocket launcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just very briefly, sir, I understand that at one point there were some accusations made that you assisted the Serbs in fact when you were in the deportation and ultimately the separation of men; is there any truth in that allegation?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Captain. I'm going to pick up where the last question ended if that's okay with you. I know it's a sensitive area but as I understand it, one of your colleagues made some sort of an allegation in the public forum that by you assisting the refugees, particularly I believe it was on the day of the 13th, the second day, especially during those early morning hours, that you in essence were participating in some sort of war crime; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He made that allegation, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact, that was so sensitive, as far as you were concerned, that you even consulted a Prosecutor to see whether you were in any jeopardy; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after that, and you learned that you were not, and -- is that right, you learned that you were not in any jeopardy, in other words there was no foundation to that claim?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, more or less the Prosecutor said that he found no ground for trying to prosecute me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly. And then after that, you also took it upon yourself to inquire whether you could launch a civil suit for defamation against your particular colleague who I believe was a lieutenant at the time?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant Rutten, I think you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was more or less in the same conversation I had with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, before coming here today, you've made several statements, as I understand it, and you've had an opportunity to sort of discuss this issue both before the ICTY and before the parliament, the parliamentary committee here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was heard in the parliamentary inquiry, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the inquiry, all right. If I could focus your attention to that inquiry, by the way before coming here today did you have an opportunity to review these documents that were generated as a result of your conversations, your discussions, your testimony?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the documents, all the documents in my possession, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So just to make sure that I'm -- that I have -- that I'm clear in my mind you have the testimony from the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay and you had a chance to look at that, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you have your testimony from the parliamentary committee inquiry that was on 11 November, 2002?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe you filled out a questionnaire for the international criminal Tribunal, the office of the Prosecution, a questionnaire that was handwritten?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what questionnaire you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that. You did give a statement to the international criminal Tribunal, the office of the Prosecution? Did you give them -- do you recall giving them a statement back in October 25, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was the statement what -- which was made in Assen. Do you mean that one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I was going to get to that too. Now, the one made in Assen was that by the Royal Netherlands Army?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: By General Van der Windt, the big briefing report, you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, and then, as I understand -- I'm going to show you these documents to make sure because we want to make sure that everybody here has them and so when I make reference to them we have a clear record if that's okay with you. Okay? But am I correct to understand that there was also some kind of inquiry or questioning done by the air force, the Royal Dutch Air Force or was that part of the same Assen inquiry?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you mean there was an operational debrief in Zagreb and there was a big debriefing in Assen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, before we get to the questioning, why don't we just get these documents, we'll get it out of the way, make our record and then we can go forward. Perhaps I could show one by one, is that -- would that be okay, Your Honour? Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, whatever you feel convenient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you -- and these have not been premarked for identification but this would be marked for identification purposes as D7, Your Honour, we left off at D6. I think there -- if you could look at that, take a look at it, and then while it's being distributed, take a glance and so we can identify it and then we move on.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the short version from the big debrief that was made in Assen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do you know whatever happened to the long version? Do you know whether you turned it over to the office of the Prosecution or?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it in my possession but not here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that falls under Rule 70 so I would object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the specific reason for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll let Mr. McCloskey explain it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this it was an internal debriefing, like an internal affairs debriefing, if you would like, and much of the material in it didn't have anything to do with these events. It all had to do with internal issues related to disciplinary issues with people or things not related, and the Dutch government went through this material and provided all the material they felt had any relevance to the war crimes issues and provided that to us for our public use, and restricted and requested that Rule 70 protections be provided to the internal versions of those reports, and so the parts that they are referring to are the internal Rule 70 designated so by the Dutch government which as you know will prevent any distribution of that material.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll accept that explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any response from Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First I'll accept that explanation Your Honour I think it's a reasonable request by the Dutch government. Surely I don't mean to pry into their internal affairs. The document does refer to Nikolic and Stalin and the other gentleman so I take it I can only trust that they redacted or gave us the portions they thought were relevant but I'll take the explanation given by the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: By the way, on this document, I don't see a date. Could you give us an approximation as to when this might have been generated, if you know?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was August, late August, of 1995, or September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the big report I think that was brought out in October or November of that same year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So might I conclude, might we conclude, that this was perhaps the first opportunity that you had to give a debriefing on this matter?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had been an operational debrief in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that was more directed to the military issues not really to the issues that were around the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it the Prosecution doesn't have that document by any chance, the Zagreb one? If that's okay, Your Honour, my asking a question here on the record?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We are not aware of it and Ms. Stewart is not aware of it and she's our expert on that manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll accept that answer as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, the next -- if I could have the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to show you what we'll mark as Defence Exhibit 8 for identification purposes. If you could look at it, please, and if you could wait until everybody has had a chance to look at it then I'll ask you a couple of questions, foundational questions, that is. Do you recognise the handwriting on this, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the handwriting as being my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we flip to page 8 of this document, that has been marked for identification purposes as Defence Exhibit 8, there is a signature. Is that your signature, sir, on the very last page at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I also note, and I was trying to figure out when this was generated, and it doesn't -- there doesn't seem to be a date, unless I've missed it somewhere?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, could I interrupt?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I saw confidential on the top of this document. Can you explain the status of this document? Is it still confidential, or is confidentiality lifted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I understand, Your Honour, all of this information has been testified to that's in this document so...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you got this document from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From the Prosecution. All of these documents are from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. McCloskey could explain to me about the status of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, these, I believe this was before my time, but I believe the OTP sent out questionnaires to the various members of DutchBat and people like the witness filled out that material to give us some of our initial guidance into the investigation so these were confidential investigative documents and that's why confidential is on the top of them, and we of course have provided them to the Defence and the information in them is still -- has some confidential nature to them. We don't object to counsel using it in his cross-examination in any way. However, Ms. Stewart has reminded me that in Krstic we offered these into evidence at times under seal when they were appropriate to be in evidence, but at this time, I do not have any objection to counsel publicly questioning the witness on these documents. It's his account and his sort of initial response to some questions related to the investigation so it's perfectly appropriate for him to be questioned on it publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To my understanding, that the confidentiality is to the public, right? If there is some information you feel that might be confidential, at any time, the parties could ask us to go into the private session. Is that agreeable?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. And perhaps if when counsel, if it's possible, well we know that he would have -- this would have been a primary document that he would ask questions of this witness. We will try to in the future make sure that there is nothing confidential but I don't believe there is, at this time, but also, the witness may help us, if he's put a family address or something on there that he might be concerned about, I'm sure he'll let us know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll endeavour to be a little more careful on these matters but I did look at it and I didn't see anything that jumped out to my attention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, is this your handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again I don't see a date. Do you have an approximation when you might have given -- put this information down?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was made up in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I have seen it since.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1995, so I've never seen it in the meanwhile but it must have been July, at the end of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, let me show you what we'll mark as Defence Exhibit number 9 for identification and see if perhaps you looked at this, seen this before. This does have a date. It says October 25, 1995. There is no signature to it but have you seen this before?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen it before. I do not remember if I ever got to see it before it was made, to sign it, so I don't remember if I have signed it on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you have an opportunity to read it, to see whether it was accurate or whether there were some, you know --

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if there were inaccuracies, I've seen a lot of reports that had a lot of inaccuracies in it but I don't remember if this was one of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you what we'll mark as Defence Exhibit 10 for identification and for the record, I'll have you identify it. Do you recognise this, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what do you recognise Defence Exhibit 10 for identification to be?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, like it says, the stenographic report of the hearing of the parliamentary inquiry committee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I take it you had an opportunity to read this as well?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Dutch and English, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Dutch and in English, and did you find anything in this report that misquoted you or that you failed to sort of accurately portray or when you --

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I remember, this is a stenographic report so --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Finally I do have your -- I have for everybody's convenience, a copy of your testimony from Krstic. As I understand it, Mr. President, that it's not necessary to mark it as an exhibit but I may be making references to it so while I have the usher up here, so that way if I do make reference to it you have it handy and I think we are about ready to begin now. Why don't we begin with the last question that was posed to you by Madam Prosecutor, and that was with respect to that allegation that had to deal with the evacuation? It's my understanding from your testimony before the parliamentary committee that the evacuation was a necessity given the situation on the ground as it existed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in fact you testified that because of the conditions, the lack of food and lack of water, and the hygiene, that an epidemic would break out then if something wasn't done; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a great danger of that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's my understanding that in your testimony you indicated that you were -- it was the best situation of the bad options that were available but nonetheless that you were pleased with the evacuation process, that it had taken place, that these people were able to get out of that miserable situation?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pleased is not the right word, I think but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You indicate -- well, you're right. And that's exactly what you say on page 7, that -- page 17, you say, well, pleased is not quite the right word but then you go on to state, page 17, you'll see, it says -- it says but it was perhaps the best of all bad options. The conditions were poor there. And then you go on to give an example and let me read it for the record: "For example, we - meaning the DutchBat - ate tinned food for four out of seven months to such an extent that people were getting stomach cramps each time they ate anything because of all the preservatives in the food. We also had hardly any fuel." And then you go on to talk about the blocking positions but then you go on to say: "In short our conditions were bad but the refugees had it much worse since they had their houses destroyed by gun fire --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "It was all a source of possible epidemics and diseases." That was your testimony, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, you go on in the next paragraph and you continue but by and large, your testimony back on 2002, was that an evacuation was absolutely necessary under the circumstances given the lack of food, the lack of water, the hygiene and what have you, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, you used the word the situation was intolerable at the time, okay? So you would not dispute me on that? You would agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree with you, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated -- you were asked about whether the refugees, whether the Muslim refugees, showed any resistance of getting on to the buses, and I believe on page 21 at the bottom of it, you say, you say, "I certainly saw," at the bottom, so the second to last, in the middle of the paragraph, "I certainly saw that the Muslim refugees did not show any resistance in getting on to the buses. They really wanted to go away on the buses. They wanted to get away from the enclave of Srebrenica." And then you were asked, you were posed another question, "Did you have to exert any force to get them to go to the buses." And your answer is: "No, we didn't do that either, we did not force anyone to get on to the buses." Right? So that's what you saw and that's what you testified to?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay? And that was correct then and it is correct today, is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you see it in the light of the events that happened in the previous days, if you are a refugee and you are shelled from your house, you have to flee, you have to take everything with you, you are separated from members of your family and you are packed with 20 to 30.000 other refugees in the sun without food and water, then I think it's understandable that you want to get away from that place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely. But I also from gather -- from the previous passage that I read, it was my impression that you had it tough and you were eating at least three squares, albeit canned foods with lots of preservatives and you were having a hard time and it was my impression that you felt that the people in Srebrenica were also under deplorable situation -- conditions as well, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Worse than our.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Worse than yours?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you go on to say -- "did you consider stopping making the evacuation?" And your answer is: "No, the picture that I got from the refugees was always -- was always that they wanted to get away from there. We did not force anybody to get on to the buses and to go away from there. In view of the danger of epidemics, breaking out, and the unhealthy situation, if people were allowed to stay there, we concluded that there was no other option than to cooperate," meaning cooperate with the Serb forces that were getting the folks on to the buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand it, from your testimony, also, that when folks were trying to get on to the buses, initially there was almost a stampede because they were trying to rush and get on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard that there was a stampede just before I arrived at that location, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of that, measures were taken to sort of slow down, slow folks down from getting on to the buses so they wouldn't hurt themselves; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fall down and be trampled on by others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday I noted, I heard you and again it was pointed out by Madam Prosecutor almost right off the bat, where you indicated that some folks were being, I believe she used the word kick, and you said you didn't see anybody getting kicked but they were being abused as they were getting on the buses, okay? Is that a fair characterisation of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, it's my understanding though from listening to you, let's take aside the one incident where you talk about the kid, you did not see any kicking of women or children at that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few incidents, the incidents I remember most clearly is the incident with the kid and most of the time when families were separated, it happened near our location, then you could see that women and the men were at some point pulled out of each other when they tried to hang on to each other and they were pulled to get them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words the wife --

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Separation, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that's a far cry from somebody being shoved and kicked on to the bus?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but those were stories I was told.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. I understand. But I just want to make sure that you with your two eyes did not see any of that activity or heard about it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And, in fact, you haven't reported it in any of your statements that you saw it so I thank you for that answer. Now, let me move on to another topic. And I want to talk to you a little bit about your mission, all right? And then we will develop from there. You arrive in Srebrenica in January, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it from hearing you yesterday before coming you took an orientation course to be a peacekeeper, not a peacemaker but a peacekeeper?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Training.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less six months of training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Because there is a different sort of mentality that a peacekeeper has to maintain than say a soldier who is battle fit and ready to go. He has to react where a peacekeeper has to stop, to think, maybe negotiate, am I correct on that?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less you have different materials. You have blue helmets instead of green, white vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And we are going to get to the blue and the green because I'm glad you mentioned that because at one point, I believe were you asked a question about whether it was a blue mission or a green mission, a blue option or a green option. And blue meaning what?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: UN, UN type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But at one point, as I understand it, you had to go into the green option, even though you were wearing the blue helmet, in other words you had to shoot at the Serbs because you felt or you were in fact perhaps getting shot at; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was for the blocking position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. For the blocking position. In fact, you were asked a question whether the blocking position was a mechanism designed to draw heat, to draw fire, as a pretext in order to get the close air protection that was needed that you were asking for during those days when it wasn't coming and eventually when it came it was too little too late; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it would be fair to say that at some point, you use yourselves more as a way of drawing some attention, drawing some fire, almost like a sitting duck, because you got that -- those white vehicles, hard to miss, right, blue helmets, people are shooting at you, then you can radio in to Zagreb, you know, send us close air protection because the situation on the ground was fairly tense; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And also making a statement that the UN was there so they couldn't get past us. That was more or less the statement we had to make.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you had a particular function while were you there, a particular mission, and you were placed in a particular area during that period; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it, you had some men behind you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, under you, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because you're an academy man, you went to the -- you're a professional soldier you went through the military academy and so you went there as a first lieutenant?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I believe you're 24 going on 25 at the time?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this was probably your first mission where you came under fire?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, one of the objectives for being there was to -- well in your own words, was to protect the militarised zone, this area, the militarised enclave, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Protect the people inside, right? And also sort of keep the new neutrality between the two acting forces?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were peacekeepers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Peacekeepers, not peacemakers.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not peacemakers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But you did have a particular function and that is you were there to ensure that the enclave was demilitarised, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was also the demilitarisation was something which we had to look at. That was being like the two parties, the Serbs and the Muslims had agreed on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well they had agreed on, thanks to the UN, and the UN got you folks in there and I believe there might have been Canadians before you got there?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And but the whole purpose was that this area, this enclave, was going to be protected by the UN and the Serbs were supposed to abide that neutrality in that zone, provided of course that that -- the people inside were totally demilitarised, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the agreement, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the agreement. But when you got there on the ground and throughout the whole period that you were there it was never demilitarised, was it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not totally, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it's like saying a little pregnant, either demilitarised or isn't, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you want to demilitarise, then you have -- you need a certain amount of soldiers. You look at the area and being that big when you have so little soldiers, then it's not possible to demilitarise it when you only have 200, 300 fighting soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But when you're talking about the 200 or 300 fighting soldiers you're talking about DutchBat, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Of course, this is 1995, it was declared demilitarised back in 1993 so I take it - and it's no fault of DutchBats but everybody that preceded you failed to keep that place demilitarised, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that the Muslims had arms, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But my question was everybody that preceded you failed to take away the weapons, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't take the weapons, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They didn't take the weapons, okay. And in fact, there were overflights coming in, helicopter flights coming in, and I believe that you observed some lights at some point, and reinforcements or at least perhaps ammunition and guns were coming in in this enclave at the same time that were you there to try to demilitarise, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard stories about that. I also read the NIOD Report but I don't know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, you don't know that for sure. However, you were able to view with your own two eyes Muslim soldiers with weapons, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some of those weapons were rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what kind of a damage could a rocket launcher do? Is it like a little pistol that you carry or is it something much more heavier?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You use it on an APC or a tank. It can do a lot of damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, so it can take out tanks?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can take out tanks when you're close enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So it's not light armour, you know, it's not like having just a rifle?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not small calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not small calibre, okay. But nonetheless --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry Your Honour. I'm sorry. I truly apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think you have to repeat from when you use it from time to time or something like this because the transcript is not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour, I'll slow it down. I'll make a conscious effort. I apologise. And I apologise to the gentleman there who must have a tough job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So, while were you there, you were able to see soldiers, Muslim soldiers, carrying rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have to state that on several occasions, we were able to take weapons from the Muslims but it was also clear to us that we didn't take all the weapons. We knew that the Muslims still had arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But that wasn't my question, now was it? My question was from time to time you would see Muslim soldiers with rocket launchers, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you had -- you had contact, not just with the Serb soldiers but you also had contact with the Muslim soldiers, as well, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understand it from your testimony today, that one of them was Naser Sabanovic?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naser Sabanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sabanovic. And what was he exactly again?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was a commander of northern -- the northern troops from the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So here you were having contact with the commander of part of the 28th division that was there, and I understand it in your contacts he tell you about some of the activities that he was carrying out, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And some of those activities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You're still too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just make a pause after the witness answers the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, so when you would meet with this gentleman, on occasions he would tell you about some of his activities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those activities entailed military activities?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going outside the enclave?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Setting mines, for instance?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he ever discuss with you any other activities such as going and burning down Serb villages or killing Serb citizens or was he just telling you about laying mines and what have you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only about the laying mines because he told me that they had information that the Serbs would try and take over my two OPs and to prevent that, he was placing mines on roads towards the enclave. That was the only stories he had told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, did you ever hear of any stories or incidents of these Muslims soldiers going out and burning down Serb villages? Did you hear any of those stories?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard stories about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it you didn't -- you don't -- you don't recollect the incident that occurred, I believe it was in June 26th, 1995, just before the events?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, these soldiers these Muslim soldiers at one time, as I understand it, from reading your testimony even pointed the rocket launchers at you during those events?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the blocking position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was in the blocking position. I believe it was the 10th or was it the 11th somewhere around there?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you folks, meaning the DutchBat, wanted to leave but the Muslim soldiers that were in the enclave pointed the rocket launchers at you to keep you there in that position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not trying to leave or we didn't have -- not have the order to leave there, but the Muslim soldiers there at that location made it quite clear by pointing the rocket launchers at our APCs that they didn't want us to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So even if you had the orders, would you have left and taken a chance at being shot at with a rocket launcher or would you have stayed just to be on the safe side?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a difficult question, I don't know. I did not have that -- that's always difficult, you have to see that when the situation occurs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, do you know off-hand by any chance how many Muslim soldiers were in the enclave in total? Because I understand you saw some of them leaving. Do you have an estimation of how many there were? If you don't know that's okay?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it you were never told by anybody?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was told but I forgot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, you indicated, sort of the last line of the questioning followed very much the same script as your first testimony with Krstic, same outline, you know, they started at the events and then they went back to April, 1995 and they wanted to question you, the Prosecutor here, questioned you about what you were able to observe with respect to the Serb soldiers in that area. Okay?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understand you correctly, your testimony is, back then as it is today, that sometime in the middle of April, you saw fresh troops arriving and I guess the older troops leaving, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The old troops also stayed, a few of the old soldiers went away. We didn't see them again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, as I understand it, it was almost like a weekly basis, every Tuesday or something the bus would come?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a weekly basis. I don't know the exact day but they had a continuing rotation, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it wasn't every Tuesday a new batch arrived the old ones stay and so you have an increase of the troops but rather a rotational basis?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first it was a rotation, and from April on, we noticed that there was a buildup in the troops. There were more troops there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know the numbers?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recollect them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now at one point, I was kind of curious about this, maybe you can help me out, you say that you made some inquiries about these folks and they said somebody told you that they were Chetniks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember no, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You can't remember whether you were told that they were Chetniks or you can't --

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember if that was told to me. I remember that there were incidents with patrols from our soldiers, from the UN, when they -- at the border crossed patrols from the Serbs, that they noticed that there were no longer the patrols they were used to meet but they were young, fresh soldiers and they made like hand signals or waving with the Serb sign of the hand and that they were more or less more aggressive than the older soldiers we were more or less used to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But my question goes back to the term Chetniks, and if I could refer you to page 2 of what has been marked as Defence Exhibit 9 for identification, that would be your witness statement of 25 October, 1995, you'll see at the second last paragraph, give us a little bit of this description, then you say and I'll read it for the record, "Until April 1995 there were somewhat older slovenly dressed Serbian soldiers here. From the end of April, 1995, the posts of the Bosnian Serb soldiers were reinforced with new personnel. This new personnel was more highly disciplined. When talking to our old regular contacts, we heard that the new soldiers were Chetniks," and I'm kind of interested if you could help me out, maybe your memory doesn't serve you well at this point but help me out first who were your old regular contacts?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please first help me, where I can find that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well it's on page 2?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness statement?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of 25 October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's the second to last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it now, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Take your time, look at it, it's the very last sentence of the second to last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The regular contacts we had from OP Romeo were the contacts from my group commanders with the Serb soldiers, the older Serb soldiers in the bunker that we called the Dragan bunker that was near OP Romeo. I don't remember the names of the Serb soldiers that were in that bunker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So are you suggesting -- are you -- are you telling us today that it was the Serbs themselves that said these are Chetniks, these new folks are Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When you say it now, that -- I remember now that they were more or less not that fond of the new soldiers because they made them clean their weapons, polish their shoes and stuff like that, shave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So the old soldiers referred to the new soldiers as Chetniks because they imposed some discipline on them, as far as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they called them Chetniks, I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a Chetnik is, by the way?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read something about it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But I was just curious why you characterised them as this in your statement, that's all. All right. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it's time for a break. Is this the right time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's a wonderful time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, before we resume, I think one matter I have to remind the counsels and the witness. Witness, I understand that you are eager to give your evidence, to help us, and I understand it's the weekend, everybody wants an early break but we have to bear in mind that whatever is said in this courtroom has to be translated into the other two languages. I don't know whether anybody in this courtroom follow in French but certainly Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Jokic are following in B/C/S. They are entitled to understand the questions and answers. So I hope -- I hope between the questions and answers, at least there will be ten seconds pause so that the interpreters and the typists will follow you. I will not act like a symphony conductor or traffic police by giving signals to the parties to indicate when to start and when to stop but I just want the proceedings in good pace. Yes, Mr. Karnavas, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Again I want to apologise to the interpreters and to the gentleman for speaking too fast and not pausing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Captain, I want to focus on the area of your understanding of the troops that were on the ground during the days of the fall of Srebrenica, particularly the 11th, 12th, 13th. It's my understanding from your previous testimony, when asked about the Drina Corps and the Drina Wolves, it was your impression and perhaps that impression you still share today, that they are one and the same. In other words, that the Drina Wolves is a nickname for the Drina Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I have read also the NIOD Report but as I remembered from the things I knew then was that by my understanding, the Drina Corps was the same as the Drina Wolves so the Drina Wolves were more or less a nickname for the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was your understanding back then?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So at some point, I believe it was the 11th, or the 12th, the 12th, you met a man by the name of Mane; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 12th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 12th. And it was your impression from speaking with him that Mane was maybe not a member of the Drina Wolves but attached or associated with or working in conjunction with the Drina Wolves, is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a member of a military police unit and like you say, attached or associated with the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So might I ask where was it that you got the impression that he was a military police? Was it through him or through some independent investigation on the ground at the time?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he told me that he was military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so I just want to make sure that we are clear to be distinguished from MUP or police that were associated with the civilian government, not special police associated with the civilian government but military police in the sense of police being within the military?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said, military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And from reading your testimonies, and your statements, it seems to me that this fellow, this Mane fellow, was quite active at the time on the ground taking care of the situation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were there on the 12th, and perhaps even on the 13th, but I know for the 12th for sure, General Mladic showed up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you referred to him yesterday as the -- as the senior officer, I believe or the highest-ranking officer. Those were your terms, I believe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for those of us who have not spent any time in the military, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That General Mladic was the soldier, the Bosnian Serb soldier, with the highest rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before that day, did you know who General Mladic was?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had seen him on television, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But did you know what his actual position was within the VRS or the BSA, as you refer to them?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
