utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know why they left it out of the big report. I only know that it was in my debriefing report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You testified today and yesterday that once you found these passports that you called to the command centre and you told them that they needed to have an escort for these buses, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's not in any of your reports about this request, is it?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was not getting into the -- in my report, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And going back to your incident with Lieutenant Rutten. Lieutenant Rutten came out the morning you were loading the buses on your own initiative and he asked you why in the world you were cooperating with these Serbs, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came in the afternoon and by then the Serbs were already there again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that his question to you, though?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it true that on page 36 of this report, that Lieutenant Rutten had expressed that you had committed a war crime?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I have no other questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, questions by Judge Vassylenko. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Have you read the book named "Srebrenica, who cares?" Which was written by Lieutenant Karremans?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read some pieces from the book but not the whole book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: What is your assessment of these pieces of the book?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've only read a few pieces but what I can deduct from that, it was a very personal story from Colonel Karremans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: I presume that you're aware of Netherlands institute documentation report on Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they have interviewed me as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And what is your assessment of this report?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a very good report that is very complete and I'm actually very glad that they could find Muslim men that, when I talk about the stage when I started, the transports, on the second day of the transportations, which was worth the discussion to a few of my colleagues. I'm very glad that they found Muslim men that escaped from the Serb net and got away from Srebrenica alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: My next question: Captain, could you describe the relations between the DutchBat and -- on the one hand, and the Serbian forces and Muslim forces on the other hand, before the tragic events in July?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were very difficult relationships. On the one hand, our unit and of course the Muslim refugees were in a terrible situation because of the Serb forces. On the other hand, we were being shot at by both parties, Serb forces as well as the Muslim forces, and we were trying to keep a peace that was not there, and maintain a truce that was no truce, but at the same time, we were speaking and looking at a big group of refugees that we could not help of -- that we could not help, as hard as we tried. So we were in the middle of groups of people that we on the other hand could not help, and the other side were shooting us. So we had difficult relations with both parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And how can you describe the relations on this crucial dates at the beginning, in the middle of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was clear to us that the Serb forces at those days were the aggressors and we wanted to stop the Serb advancement. We -- I was confronted with Muslim soldiers when I was standing in the blocking position, which refused to help the Muslim refugees that were not able to walk any more, to flee to the north. So we tried to take as much as we could on our APC and in our APCs, and our main concern on that, in those days, was the fate of the refugees, and trying to keep an area under our control, more or less, as a safe area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Captain, have you ever met or contacted the accused in this case, Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Jokic, as well as Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Nikolic at that time?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not that I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: The last question: Have you any idea why the Serb captain or major or platoon commander was nicknamed Stalin?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Who nicknamed him? The DutchBat or the Muslims or the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He was nicknamed by the Serbs themselves and he used it maybe as it was just a code name on the radio, but the Serbs -- it was a name given by the Serbs themselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. I have no questions. Thank you, Captain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Judge Argibay, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Good even evening, Captain. I have only one question and it's a clarification. When you were talking about trying to get escort or accompanying the buses in the last day and you said you radioed your headquarters, had you had any answer on that point from the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations officer from our battalion headquarters said he was trying everything he could to escort the buses, and in that chaotic situation, that was the best possible answer I could expect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Did you get reinforcements or something?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did in the get reinforcements. At that time we did not need reinforcements. We just needed vehicles with UN soldiers in them to escort the buses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Did you get them?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not get them, and I don't know if the buses were accompanied by the UN, but I heard that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ARGIBAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Captain. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions out of Judges' questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do have a couple of questions. Further cross-examination by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is in respect to the answer that you gave to Judge Vassylenko's question about the relationships and you indicated the situation was bad because of the Serb forces. That's your understanding, right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because our convoys did not get clearance from the Serb forces, that was the main reason why we had lack of food, medical supplies, and all the things we needed for hygiene and stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In the Krstic trial, according to the judgement rendered in that case, in paragraph 30 of the judgement, it indicates that on the morning of the 26th of June, 1995, there was a raid by Muslim military on to a Serb village where they ended up burning some houses and killing some Serbs. Don't you think that that would somehow exacerbate the situation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I gave you a chance to ask some questions but the scope should be within the questions asked by the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that this question is out of the scope of Judge Vassylenko's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well but with all due respect, Your Honour, the answer that was given, there seems to be a total blame of the situation in Srebrenica because of the Serb forces, and obviously his answer is that there was a -- the Serbs were preventing humanitarian aid or food aid from going in. That's one part of the equation. The other part of the equation might be that the Muslim forces were using the enclave as a staging ground to commit atrocities and that might be also the reason why some of the aid wasn't or the food wasn't going into the enclave and I'm merely pointing out whether he was aware of this or not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, this issue has been debated for many times and the witness of course has his own view. If you have a different case, I think at a later stage, you may cross other witnesses or you could present your evidence in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour I have a couple of questions. Further cross-examination by Ms. Sinatra:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Lieutenant, based on one of the questions about you moving the refugees from the blocking point to the safety of Potocari, whatever that might have been at the time, you did state just then that the Muslim forces refused to help the refugees fleeing at that time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And going back to the question about your radio contact on the 13th, after all of the transport had left, you called back to central command and you said it's very important that we have escorts with these buses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEENDERT CORNELIS VAN DUIJN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That request was not in any of your reports and at that time, you never mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Sinatra, this question is also outside of the scope of Judge Vassylenko's question. I'm not going to give you another chance for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just trying to clarify the communications, the time that that telephone --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object at this point they are using this to grandstand in order to condemn this man personally. It's outrageous, I would strongly object to it. Enough is enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I'm not going to compete with Mr. McCloskey for grandstanding but I would like to thank the witness I think he's a brave soldier and I really have empathy for the position they were in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may for the record. I do take offence to Mr. McCloskey's comment. He used "they." Nobody is grandstanding and there is a proper way of objecting and I think it's totally inappropriate and nobody is trying to demean this individual or to embarrass him and if that's his characterisation, then he can keep it to himself or he can object in a proper form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure whether this "they" is including you or not. Any way, at this stage are there any documents to tender from the Prosecution side?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll be tendering Exhibits 51 through 56 as well as the last exhibit which I think is correctly marked as 2.6/A. I think I incorrectly referred to it as 20.6 earlier. It's actually 2.6/A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this correction. Any objections? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So those documents are admitted into evidence. Are there any documents that the Defence team would like to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, in keeping with your earlier -- I mean normally I would tender everything I submitted but I leave it up to the Trial Chamber to decide but I understand that your earlier order was that these sorts of documents, because they are quote unquote hearsay, need not come in if the witness has testified from them so the answer is I think I would tender them but I understand your previous ruling and I would abide by that ruling and I suspect that the Prosecution is going to be jumping up and down objecting to the hearsay nature of these documents any way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, on the same grounds we objected to with respect to the other witness. As Your Honour indicated earlier this witness has testified live and it's not necessary to tender these documents at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure it's about that report of the hearings of parliamentary committee.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: There is no objection with respect to that report, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So this document, document D10/1 is admitted into evidence. Any documents that the Defence of Mr. Jokic would like to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we would just like the record to reflect that D10/1 would also reflect our impeachment the witness also as a D2 document also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's possible. Thank you very much. Witness, thank you very much for coming to give your evidence and we all wish you good luck. The usher will show you out of the room. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we still have a few minutes left so there are several issues I would like to discuss with counsels. The first matter is about the counsel issues. At the beginning of this sitting, this afternoon, Mr. Blagojevic raised the issue of the fair representation. We believe that this Trial Chamber has made a decision to this effect, and this Trial Chamber has already informed Mr. Blagojevic that if he could seek certification for leave to appeal this decision, if he's not satisfied with it. We also have been informed that the independent counsel will discuss this matter with Mr. Blagojevic on Monday and Tuesday, and we are also informed that the translation into the B/C/S of that decision has been distributed. According to Rule 73, the time period for the application of certification to this Trial Chamber will start from yesterday, which means from yesterday, there will be seven days, within the seven days Mr. Blagojevic, after consulting the independent counsel assigned by this Chamber, could file an application for certification to appeal this decision. And this Trial Chamber will render its decision whether to permit the certification in seven days. After rendering this decision, Mr. Blagojevic and his independent counsel also have seven days to file their appeal to the Appeals Chamber on the substance. So I believe there are plenty of time for them to discuss this matter and to prepare the appeal. After filing of the appeal, I believe, if I'm wrong, somebody could correct me, I believe that Mr. Karnavas also has the right to file a reply to the Appeals Chamber. It is our intention to continue to finish hearing of the witnesses in that witness list before the summer recess, because this Trial Chamber has made a decision in this aspect and will abide by it, unless a decision made by the Appeals Chamber says otherwise. There is one matter I would like to bring to the attention of both parties. That is as we understand it, the first group of witnesses, of sort of the background witnesses, and after the first group of witnesses, we will have some more substantial witnesses in this case. Pending the decision of the Appeals Chamber concerning the counsel issues, are we going to proceed despite any decisions by the Appeals Chamber or we just delay the hearings until the picture is more clear? Any comments from the parties? We are not going to make a decision. I'm just going to hear the initial response from the parties. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's clear to the Prosecution that the Trial Chamber and everyone, Mr. Karnavas and all are trying to work a solution to this, and the question you pose is the difficult question. We will give it some very serious thought and try to have a response for you, and I think what is also clear to the record is that Mr. Karnavas is available and ready to speak to his client and that his client would be well served to speak to him, and that what's going on here is the client's, as the Court showed in one of its rulings, is the client has chosen this muteness. The Prosecution, of course, would prefer that they are able to speak to each other so that we can get on with it. Because we would prefer to get on with it. We also do not want to come back again. So we will consider this critical question about the Appellate Chamber and perhaps the Appellate Chamber could give us an idea of how much time it may take them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the position that I find myself in, when I say I, meaning myself and Ms. Tomanovic, I don't think it's appropriate for me to voice an opinion on this matter. And so I will do whatever the Court instructs me to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the team for Mr. Jokic will take no position in this decision dealing with the counsel for Blagojevic but if the Court would allow me to address the upcoming witnesses, Obrenovic and Nikolic, after you finish this, I would like to address that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: May I do it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. I know that the Prosecution has said that they are going to bring Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Nikolic to testify after the break in August. As Defence counsels, Mr. Stojanovic and I for Mr. Jokic, we cannot be prepared to cross-examine Mr. Obrenovic at that time. We have not received any funds from the Registry. We cannot pursue investigations in the Zvornik area to find witnesses that will give us information and support any positions that we might have on cross-examination of the most important witness to come to testify against Mr. Jokic. I think that in all fairness and as far as due process goes for Mr. Jokic, we ask and implore this Court to postpone that testimony until we get some funds from the Registry in order to secure investigations back in the Zvornik area and we cannot be prepared between now and then. We have not initiated an investigation at this point because we have no funds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that's another matter. I certainly will convey your idea to the Registry but I'm not sure what the results will be. In this case, anyway, I believe that Mr. Jokic is not a party to this dispute but is an affected third party because he has the right to have a fair and expeditious trial. Mr. Blagojevic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Blagojevic? Do you have something to say to this matter? Have you got translation in B/C/S of the decision made by this Trial Chamber? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yesterday I have not had time to read it but I now have enough time in light of the procedure that you have just explained, Your Honour, to do it. I believe I will be able to respect the procedure that you have suggested and I don't think that there is any need to say anything else on the subject, but just to let you know that I still abide by my position, but to be perfectly frank, I have thought about the matter thoroughly and with full responsibility, but at the end of the game, I must say that I am disappointed with the rootless, irresponsible accusation for criminal behaviour on my account by the person who is supposed to defend me in this very difficult and complex case. I know that this feeling of disappointment is a separate issue and have nothing to do with the documents that actually led me to lose my trust in the previously appointed counsel. I have lost all hope in his ability to be objective, reasonable and to lead my defence in a rational and responsible way through this trial. This trust cannot be restored in any way. There are no elements whatsoever for such a position. And in order to clear my mind, in order to dispel this confusion, I am compelled to seek for another solution. I do not intend to defend myself on my own. I'm not qualified for that. I'm not capable for that. I need to choose a professional, a man who will be able to represent me with full responsibility, professionally and with credibility. I do not have anything else to add, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for your statement. You may sit down, please. You have to remember that this Trial Chamber said clearly that we encourage you to rebuild your relationship with Mr. Karnavas and Ms. Tomanovic because we believe through our decision they are still your counsel. And I would like also to inform you that if you do in the appeal this decision to the Appeals Chamber, our decision will be final. Now, during the past few days, I believe Mr. Karnavas did a good job. He vigorously defended your interests, effectively cross-examined the witnesses, and tendered some important documents into evidence. Of course, there are some problems on his part. I'll come to it later. But I believe that he could do his job well. There is nothing impossible in this world. Well, Mr. McCloskey, you said that you'll come back to this issue later. You mean that you'll file something in written form. The first thing I have to make clear is whenever we finish the first group of witnesses, we will not hear any more witnesses before the summer recess. We are talking about the period after the summer recess. Are you going to file something in this aspect?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as I've had a chance to just think and sit and listen a bit, and to everyone, and considering the importance of the post-recess evidence, though I also -- we will hear from the survivors in the next few weeks, I think -- as reluctant as I am to stop again, because I think we are beginning to get a good rhythm in going forward, I think out of an abundance of caution and safety for the record I think it would be best to have the Appellate Chamber review this matter and come to the quickest and fairest possible decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you whether you're going to file a written comments or statements in this aspect or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, should Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Sjocrona file a vigorous appeal that will address the issues before the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution may not have any need to enter this particular fray. Our concern is that these issues, and they are important, they are serious and they need to be carefully dealt with by the Trial Chamber and our interest of course in it is the fact that we do not want to ask these witnesses to testify again. As for the conflict between counsel and these issues we have made our position initially clear. However, we are not privy to all the important documents, nor do I think it appropriate that we should be. In that respect, we may very well side step -- step aside on this issue and allow the parties to sort it out. If we find that the issue is not going to be appealed or that it is not appropriately dealt with, we may very well want to add something in order that the Appellate Chamber be fully briefed on the issue so that they can make the best ruling possible. We may suggest in that regard that our deadline for filing a request for certification of appeal be one or two days after the deadline of the others, that it would allow us to look at their documents and it would be my feeling at this time, having seen some of the legal work that has come out of Mr. Sjocrona, that he's very capable of filing a response that will cover the appropriate issues, and I know Mr. Karnavas will do the same, and in that case, the Office of the Prosecutor need not be involved, and that would be my first choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, maybe I did not make myself clear. I think we are talking about different things. You are talking about the appeal on the Trial Chamber's decision. And I'm talking about the scheduling arrangements after the summer recess. As the first issue, I did not look into the jurisprudence of this Tribunal, but if Mr. Blagojevic or his independent counsel did not appeal, I don't think you have the right to appeal, because you are not a party. The party to this dispute. You are -- I think your status is more or less the same with Ms. Sinatra, with Mr. Jokic. You are affected third party but not the party to that dispute. So I wonder where is your standing to this case, to this issue, if Mr. Blagojevic does not appeal? This is the first issue. Maybe I'm wrong. The second issue is my concern is pending the decision of the Appeals Chamber on the counsel issues, are we going to continue to sit or we just make a short period delay waiting for the decision from the Appeals Chamber? This is the second issue. What I want is your response to the second issue, but not the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Understood, Mr. President. I don't think we need to file anything unless you would like us to on that issue. I can state today that I think it would be best to have a stay of the proceedings so that we can get a clear roadmap from the Appellate Chamber and then go full speed ahead when we get that. That would be my -- we thought quite a bit about this actually and I did want to take into account what everyone is saying and with Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Nikolic testifying, and other -- Mr. Butler and some of the other witnesses, it probably would be the best approach.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's a very clear answer. Thank you. There are some comments from this bench. Yes, any problem, Mr. Blagojevic? THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just would like to clarify something for myself. These deadlines that you have listed here, do they obligate Mr. Sjocrona or me, or am I supposed to act upon these deadlines regardless of the obligation of Mr. Sjocrona considering that he's an independent counsel who has been appointed, then he should be -- this should be binding for him. However, if his appointment has ceased because the way I've understood it in a way his appointment has been suspended, the representatives in the Registry have told me that he has stopped acting on my behalf, then am I supposed to do this by myself, to file an appeal by myself? I can try and find my way in this because I would like to appeal but I would like the independent counsel, this one or another one, I would like him to fulfil the task of Mr. Sjocrona, that somehow this can be resolved and terminated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much to bring to our attention about your concern on this issue. First of all, I can assure you that the independent counsel's mandate will continue and it will cover the whole period of the appeal. I'm pretty sure about it. And you could discuss this matter with Mr. Sjocrona next Monday or Tuesday, and discuss your -- any actions you would like to take. Secondly, I can assure you that, as I did before, that this Trial Chamber will extend the period of time for you to seek certification until after you have a chance to read the decision and to discuss it with the independent counsel. So I believe, theoretically speaking, those time limits applied to you and to your independent counsel, but you need more time, please feel free to let us know. We could extend the time period for your preparation of that application for appeal. Thank you. There are some comments from this bench at the conclusion of the four testimonies. Normally we do not make comments about the presentation of the case, the direct examination or cross-examination but we found it necessary to take this opportunity to share some observations and comments with the parties. First, we believe that the witness who came to testify in this Tribunal must be treated with dignity and respect. The Trial Chamber will not tolerate the retraumatisation of these individuals for the purpose of Prosecution or in the names of Defence. I think I have mentioned that before. I will not repeat it. The purpose of this trial is to determine the individual criminal responsibility of two persons, Mr. Blagojevic and Mr. Jokic. While other persons have been indicted for crimes in and around Srebrenica during the course of the war in that area, this trial is to determine only whether the acts and omissions of these two individuals warrant a finding of guilty or not guilty of the crimes alleged in the indictment. While the indictment in this case is focused on the summer and fall, 1995, the Trial Chamber appreciates that some historical background and the context may be useful to its full understanding of the charges. It is not however an invitation to raise crimes committed by others or prior events as the justification for any criminal act. Questions to this effect will not be permitted. Finally, this Trial Chamber would like to draw the attention of the counsels from both sides, the differences between this Tribunal and any domestic jurisdictions. In this Tribunal, judges and not jury, are the finders of fact. The Trial Chamber would like to advise all counsels to take this into account when considering the substance and even the style of their submissions, examinations, conduct, before the Trial Chamber. And those comments are applicable to both parties. Later on, we'll have some victim witnesses. I hope both parties will bear that in mind. At this stage, is there anything that the parties would like to bring to the attention of this bench? Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, is this a good time to talk about the dates for the summer recess? That was something we talked to your counsel about or we can just -- it's getting late, maybe we cannot worry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you want to say something, yes, say it publicly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Given some of the -- specifically that Mr. Obrenovic now will be testifying after the break, along with Mr. Nikolic and others, I think there is an additional work load on everyone and that I think -- I know that counsel for both Jokic and Blagojevic would appreciate, with the Prosecution, to start up again the first week of September as opposed to I believe August 25th. That would give us all a little more room to get our work done and as you know there has been some additional documents that are being translated that I think all the parties need to take a look at, and I think Ms. Sinatra has mentioned some other work that they need to have done. And that one week would be very helpful for us to get started. Of course this is in addition to the problem we've already discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any comments or response? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would concur with the Prosecutor on this issue. We do have some additional work. We are -- this is the Nikolic Obrenovic issues have put a bit of strain on our resources, physical resources, I should say, not financial, so I think it would be worthwhile and in keeping with what's going to be happening with the appeal, I think it all makes sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to join to what has been proposed, Your Honours, but bearing in mind the importance for the Defence of Dragan Jokic, the testimony of Dragan Obrenovic and the evidence that we received a few days ago from the Prosecutor's Office, it wouldn't be a bad idea to even delay the time even further of starting after the recess. However, considering what you've -- from the -- everything that's been said, perhaps this will happen in any case for some other reasons so there could be a solution found in all this when we are speaking about the time that the trial will restart after the recess. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are not in the position to make a ruling at this moment but we'll take into consideration all the submissions by the parties and we'll render a scheduling order to this effect one week or two weeks before the recess. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 6.54 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of July, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
